tools.name: automation_create_workflow
tools.description:
Create a new visual automation workflow with UNIQUE IMMUTABLE SLUG.

=== CRITICAL WORKFLOW CREATION GUIDE ===

## SLUG SYSTEM (MANDATORY)
Format: wf_<8random>_<timestamp>
Example: wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847
- NOT title-based (titles can change)
- Immutable identifier (never changes)
- Auto-generated by backend
- Use for referencing workflows

## STRUCTURE
TRIGGER: What starts the workflow
  - manual: User clicks "Run"
  - schedule: Cron-based (e.g., "0 9 * * *" = daily 9am)
  - webhook: External API call
  - event: Platform event (gmail_new_message, etc.)

ACTIONS: Sequence of tool executions
  - tool: Tool name from 594-tool library
  - parameters: Tool parameters (can use {{placeholders}})
  - condition: Optional execution condition

PLACEHOLDERS: Data flow between steps
  - {{emails}} = Output from previous step
  - {{user_input}} = Data at execution time
  - {{trigger.data}} = Trigger event data
  - {{date}}, {{timestamp}} = Current date/time

CATEGORIES: email, data_processing, notifications, scheduling, crm, accounting, other

## CRON PATTERNS
"0 9 * * *"      = Daily at 9am
"0 */2 * * *"    = Every 2 hours
"0 9 * * 1"      = Every Monday 9am
"0 0 1 * *"      = First day of month
"*/15 * * * *"   = Every 15 minutes

## EXAMPLE REQUEST
User: "Email me a summary of unread Gmail messages every morning at 9am"

Your Response:
automation_create_workflow(
    title="Daily Gmail Summary",
    description="Get unread emails, summarize, and send digest",
    trigger={
        "type": "schedule",
        "schedule_cron": "0 9 * * *"
    },
    actions=[
        {
            "tool": "gmail_list_messages",
            "parameters": {"max_results": 20, "query": "is:unread"}
        },
        {
            "tool": "ai_summarize_text",
            "parameters": {"text": "{{emails}}", "max_length": 500}
        },
        {
            "tool": "gmail_send_email",
            "parameters": {
                "to": "user@example.com",
                "subject": "Daily Summary",
                "body": "{{summary}}"
            }
        }
    ],
    category="email"
)

## YOUR RESPONSE TO USER
Explain clearly:
1. Workflow created with unique slug: wf_k7m3p9x2_1732125847
2. What it does (trigger + actions)
3. How to use it (execute manually, schedule, link to thread)
4. Slug is draggable into chat

## WORKFLOW LIFECYCLE
1. Create → automation_create_workflow()
2. Schedule → automation_schedule_workflow(slug, cron)
3. Execute → automation_execute_workflow(slug, input_data)
4. Monitor → automation_get_execution_history(slug)
5. Pause → automation_deactivate_workflow(slug)
6. Delete → automation_delete_workflow(slug)

## VISUAL FLOW (AUTO-GENERATED)
Backend creates nodes/connections:
- Hexagon (green) = Trigger
- Rectangle (blue) = Action
- Diamond (orange) = Conditional
- Connections = Sequential flow

Returns: automation_id, slug, visual_flow_json, execution_prompt

schedule_cron.description: Cron expression for scheduled triggers (e.g., '0 9 * * *' for daily at 9am)

parameters.description: Tool parameters (can include {{placeholders}} from previous steps)

condition.description: Optional condition to execute this action (e.g., '{{email.from}} == boss@company.com')

returns.description: Created workflow with automation_id, slug, and visual representation

parameters.title: Gmail to Sheets
parameters.description: Save new Gmail messages to Google Sheets

tools.name: automation_update_workflow
tools.description:
Update an existing workflow by slug - add/remove actions, modify trigger, change parameters. UI automatically refreshes canvas after update.

=== CRITICAL UPDATE GUIDE ===

## WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL
User says ANY of these with an existing workflow slug:
- 'add an action/step to workflow wf_xxx'
- 'remove the email step from wf_xxx'
- 'change the schedule to daily'
- 'update the trigger'
- 'modify parameters in step 3'
- 'insert action between steps 2 and 3'

## REQUIRED: Must have workflow slug (wf_<8random>_<timestamp>)

## UPDATE OPERATIONS

### 1. ADD ACTIONS
add_actions: [
    {
        "tool": "gmail_send_email",
        "parameters": {"to": "user@example.com", "subject": "Alert"},
        "position": 3  # Insert at position 3 (optional, default: append to end)
    }
]

### 2. REMOVE ACTIONS
remove_actions: [0, 2]  # Remove actions at positions 0 and 2

### 3. UPDATE TRIGGER
update_trigger: {
    "type": "schedule",
    "schedule_cron": "0 */2 * * *"  # Change to every 2 hours
}

### 4. UPDATE ACTION PARAMETERS
update_action_parameters: {
    "position": 1,  # Action at position 1
    "parameters": {
        "max_results": 50  # Change max_results from 20 to 50
    }
}

### 5. UPDATE TITLE/DESCRIPTION
update_metadata: {
    "title": "New Workflow Title",
    "description": "Updated description"
}

## EXAMPLE REQUESTS

**User:** "Add an email notification to workflow wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847"
**AI Call:**
automation_update_workflow(
    slug="wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847",
    add_actions=[{
        "tool": "gmail_send_email",
        "parameters": {
            "to": "user@example.com",
            "subject": "Workflow Complete",
            "body": "{{summary}}"
        }
    }]
)

**User:** "Change the schedule to every 2 hours"
**AI Call:**
automation_update_workflow(
    slug="wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847",
    update_trigger={
        "type": "schedule",
        "schedule_cron": "0 */2 * * *"
    }
)

**User:** "Remove the first step"
**AI Call:**
automation_update_workflow(
    slug="wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847",
    remove_actions=[0]
)

## RESPONSE TO USER
After successful update:
1. Confirm what changed: 'Added email notification action to your workflow'
2. Explain update: 'The workflow now sends you an email after processing'
3. Note: 'The UI canvas has automatically refreshed to show the new action'
4. If scheduled: 'Next run: <time>'

## AUTO-REFRESH UI
After update completes, backend sends WebSocket message to frontend:
- Frontend automatically reloads workflow JSON
- Canvas re-renders with updated nodes/connections
- User sees changes immediately without manual refresh

## ERROR HANDLING
- Invalid slug: 'Workflow wf_xxx not found'
- Invalid position: 'Cannot insert at position 10 (workflow has 5 actions)'
- Invalid tool name: 'Tool xyz_invalid_tool not found in 594-tool library'
- Missing required params: 'Action gmail_send_email requires parameter: to'

position.description: Insert at this position (optional, default: append to end)

remove_actions.description: Array of action positions to remove (e.g., [0, 2] removes actions at positions 0 and 2)

returns.description: Updated workflow with new action count, visual_flow_json, and confirmation message

tools.name: automation_list_workflows
tools.description:
List all saved automation workflows for the user. Returns workflows with metadata, status, and execution counts.

USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use this when user asks 'show me my workflows', 'list automations', 'what workflows do I have?'
- Filter by category to narrow results (e.g., category='email' for email workflows)
- Filter by status to show active/inactive/draft workflows
- Default returns all workflows (limit 50)
- Response includes: automation_id, slug, title, status, category, trigger_type, action_count, execution_count, last_run, created_at
- Use slug from results to perform operations (execute, schedule, etc.)

EXAMPLE RESPONSE TO USER:
'You have 3 active workflows:
1. Daily Gmail Summary (wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847) - Scheduled: 0 9 * * * - Last run: 2h ago (success)
2. Invoice Processing (wf_k7m3p9x2_1732125847) - Manual trigger - 15 executions
3. Slack Notifications (wf_x9y2z5a1_1732200123) - Event: shopify_new_order - Active'

COMMON PARAMETERS:
- No parameters = List all workflows
- category='email' = Email workflows only
- status='active' = Active workflows only
- limit=10 = Show 10 most recent

tools.name: automation_get_workflow
tools.description:
Get detailed workflow information including visual flow, execution history, and configuration.

USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use this when user wants details about a specific workflow (e.g., 'show me the email workflow', 'tell me about wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847')
- Accepts either automation_id (numeric) or slug (wf_xxx format)
- Returns complete workflow structure: trigger config, action sequence, visual nodes/connections, execution stats
- Use this before explaining how a workflow works or suggesting modifications

RESPONSE INCLUDES:
- automation_id, slug, title, description, category
- trigger: {type, schedule_cron, event_type}
- actions: [{tool, parameters, condition}, ...]
- ui_json: {shapes: [nodes], connections: [arrows]}
- execution_json: {steps: [executable actions]}
- status, created_at, updated_at, last_execution
- execution_count, success_rate

EXAMPLE RESPONSE TO USER:
'Here's your Daily Gmail Summary workflow (wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847):

**Trigger:** Schedule (Every day at 9:00 AM)
**Actions:**
1. Get unread Gmail messages (max 20)
2. Summarize with AI (max 500 chars)
3. Send summary email to you

**Status:** Active - Last run: 2h ago (success) - 45 total executions (95.6% success rate)'

COMMON USE CASES:
- User asks 'how does this workflow work?'
- User drags workflow slug into chat
- Before modifying workflow (get current state first)

returns.description: Workflow details with nodes, connections, and execution data

tools.name: automation_execute_workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow immediately (manual trigger). Returns execution ID for tracking progress.

USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use this when user says 'run this workflow', 'execute the automation', 'test this now'
- Accepts workflow slug (wf_xxx) or automation_id
- Optionally provide input_data for {{user_input}} placeholders (e.g., {"spreadsheet_id": "abc123"})
- Link execution to thread_id to track in conversation
- Returns execution_id for monitoring progress

EXECUTION FLOW:
1. Validates workflow exists and has actions
2. Resolves placeholders ({{user_input}}, {{date}}, {{timestamp}})
3. Executes actions sequentially
4. Each action output becomes available to next action as {{previous_output}}
5. Returns final status (success/failure) and all step results

EXAMPLE RESPONSE TO USER:
'Running your Daily Gmail Summary workflow...

Execution ID: exec_12345
Status: Running

✓ Step 1: Retrieved 8 unread emails
✓ Step 2: Generated summary (245 chars)
✓ Step 3: Sent email to you

Execution completed in 4.2 seconds'

COMMON PARAMETERS:
- automation_id='wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847' (required)
- input_data={"email": "user@example.com"} (optional, for {{user_input}})
- thread_id=123 (optional, links to conversation)

ERROR HANDLING:
- If step fails, execution stops and returns error details
- Use automation_get_execution_history() to see full error logs
- Suggest fixes based on error message (missing credentials, invalid parameters, etc.)

automation_id.description: Workflow ID or slug to execute

input_data.description: Optional input data to pass to workflow (replaces {{user_input}} placeholders)

thread_id.description: Optional thread ID to associate execution with conversation

returns.description: Execution result with execution_id, status, and output

tools.name: automation_schedule_workflow
tools.description:
Schedule a workflow to run automatically at specified times or events. Activates the automation.

USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use this when user says 'schedule this workflow', 'run this every hour', 'activate this automation'
- Requires cron expression for schedule (see platform_guide for common patterns)
- Sets workflow status to 'active' and creates background scheduler task
- Workflow will execute automatically at specified times
- Optional timezone parameter (default: UTC)

CRON EXPRESSION GUIDE:
- '0 9 * * *' = Daily at 9:00 AM
- '0 */2 * * *' = Every 2 hours
- '*/15 * * * *' = Every 15 minutes
- '0 9 * * 1' = Every Monday at 9:00 AM
- '0 0 1 * *' = First day of month at midnight

EXAMPLE RESPONSE TO USER:
'Your Daily Gmail Summary workflow is now scheduled!

⏰ Schedule: Every day at 9:00 AM (UTC)
📅 Next run: Tomorrow at 9:00 AM
🔄 Recurring: Daily
✓ Status: Active

I'll automatically run this workflow every morning and send you the email summary.'

COMMON USE CASES:
- Daily reports (0 9 * * *)
- Hourly data sync (0 */1 * * *)
- Weekly summaries (0 9 * * 1)
- Monthly invoices (0 0 1 * *)

VALIDATION:
- Backend validates cron expression syntax
- Calculates next run time and shows to user
- Creates scheduler_task_id for tracking

schedule_cron.description: Cron expression (e.g., '0 9 * * *' = daily at 9am, '0 */2 * * *' = every 2 hours)

tools.name: automation_deactivate_workflow
tools.description:
Deactivate a scheduled workflow. Stops automatic execution but preserves the workflow.

USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use this when user says 'pause this workflow', 'stop the automation', 'deactivate this'
- Stops scheduled execution immediately
- Workflow remains in database (can be reactivated later)
- Does NOT delete workflow or execution history
- Status changes from 'active' to 'inactive'

EXAMPLE RESPONSE TO USER:
'Your Daily Gmail Summary workflow has been deactivated.

⏸️ Status: Inactive
📊 Total executions: 45 (95.6% success)
🕐 Last run: 2 hours ago (success)

The workflow is paused and won't run automatically. You can:
- Reactivate it with automation_schedule_workflow()
- Run it manually with automation_execute_workflow()
- Delete it permanently with automation_delete_workflow()'

COMMON USE CASES:
- User wants to pause workflow temporarily
- Workflow needs modifications before next run
- Testing period is over
- User is away and doesn't need automated runs

REACTIVATION:
- Call automation_schedule_workflow() with same cron to reactivate
- All workflow settings and history are preserved

tools.name: automation_delete_workflow
tools.description:
Delete a workflow permanently. This cannot be undone.

USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use this when user says 'delete this workflow', 'remove the automation', 'I don't need this anymore'
- PERMANENT deletion - cannot be recovered
- Removes workflow, execution history, and scheduler tasks
- Ask for confirmation before executing (this is destructive)

CONFIRMATION PATTERN:
1. User requests deletion
2. AI responds: 'Are you sure you want to delete [Workflow Title] (wf_xxx)? This will:
   - Delete the workflow permanently
   - Remove all execution history (X runs)
   - Stop any scheduled executions
   
   This cannot be undone. Reply "yes delete" to confirm.'
3. User confirms
4. AI executes automation_delete_workflow()

EXAMPLE RESPONSE TO USER:
'Your Daily Gmail Summary workflow (wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847) has been deleted permanently.

🗑️ Removed:
- Workflow configuration
- 45 execution records
- Scheduled task (daily at 9:00 AM)

The workflow cannot be recovered. If you need similar functionality, you can create a new workflow.'

ALTERNATIVE SUGGESTION:
- If user might need workflow later, suggest automation_deactivate_workflow() instead
- Deactivation preserves workflow for future reactivation
- Deletion is only for workflows user is certain they won't use again

WARNING:
- Always confirm before deleting
- Explain what will be lost (execution history, schedule)
- Suggest export with automation_export_workflow() for backup

tools.name: automation_get_execution_history
tools.description:
Get execution history for a workflow. Shows past runs, success/failure, duration, and errors.

USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use this when user asks 'how is my workflow doing?', 'show me the execution history', 'when did this last run?', 'did it fail?'
- Returns chronological list of executions with detailed results
- Filter by status (success/failure/running) to debug issues
- Default limit is 20 executions (configurable)
- Each execution includes: execution_id, timestamp, duration, status, step results, error messages

RESPONSE STRUCTURE:
- execution_id: Unique identifier for this run
- started_at: ISO timestamp when execution began
- completed_at: ISO timestamp when execution finished
- duration_seconds: How long execution took
- status: 'success', 'failure', or 'running'
- steps: Array of step results with tool name, parameters used, output, duration
- error: Error message if status='failure'
- trigger_type: 'manual', 'schedule', 'webhook', or 'event'

EXAMPLE RESPONSE TO USER:
'Here's the execution history for Daily Gmail Summary (last 10 runs):

✓ Today 9:00 AM - Success (4.2s) - 8 emails processed
✓ Yesterday 9:00 AM - Success (3.8s) - 12 emails processed
✗ Nov 18 9:00 AM - Failed (1.2s) - Error: Gmail API rate limit exceeded
✓ Nov 17 9:00 AM - Success (4.5s) - 5 emails processed
✓ Nov 16 9:00 AM - Success (3.9s) - 15 emails processed

**Success Rate:** 80% (8/10 successful)
**Average Duration:** 3.9 seconds'

COMMON PARAMETERS:
- automation_id='wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847' (required)
- limit=10 (show 10 most recent)
- status_filter='failure' (show only failures for debugging)

DEBUGGING WITH HISTORY:
- If user reports workflow not working, fetch history with status_filter='failure'
- Analyze error messages to identify issue (credentials, API limits, invalid parameters)
- Suggest fixes based on error patterns
- Show success rate to assess reliability

returns.description: List of executions with timestamps, status, and results

tools.name: automation_export_workflow
tools.description:
Export workflow as JSON for backup, sharing, or import into another system.

USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use this when user says 'export this workflow', 'backup my automation', 'share this workflow', 'download as JSON'
- Returns complete workflow structure as JSON
- Optionally include execution history (default: false)
- Exported JSON can be saved to file, shared with others, or imported into another system
- Preserves all workflow configuration: trigger, actions, placeholders, visual layout

EXPORT INCLUDES:
- automation_id, slug, title, description, category
- trigger configuration (type, cron, event)
- actions array with tool names and parameters
- ui_json with visual canvas layout (shapes, connections)
- execution_json with executable steps
- created_at, updated_at metadata
- (optional) execution_history array if include_history=true

EXAMPLE RESPONSE TO USER:
'Here's the export for your Daily Gmail Summary workflow:

```json
{
  "automation_id": 42,
  "slug": "wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847",
  "title": "Daily Gmail Summary",
  "trigger": {"type": "schedule", "schedule_cron": "0 9 * * *"},
  "actions": [...],
  "ui_json": {...},
  "execution_json": {...}
}
```

You can save this JSON to a file or share it with others. To restore, use automation_import_workflow() (if available) or recreate with automation_create_workflow().'

COMMON USE CASES:
- Backup before making changes
- Share workflow template with team
- Migrate workflow to another account/system
- Version control for workflow configurations
- Document workflow structure

PARAMETERS:
- automation_id='wf_xxx' (required)
- include_history=true (optional, adds execution logs to export)

tools.description:
Publish a draft workflow as a live automation. Validates workflow structure, activates it for execution, optionally schedules it with cron expression, and links it to the current thread. Use this when user says 'publish this workflow', 'activate the automation', 'make this live', or 'schedule this to run'.

USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use this after user finishes building workflow in canvas
- Validates workflow structure (has trigger, has actions, no errors)
- Changes status from 'draft' to 'active'
- Optionally creates schedule with cron expression
- Links workflow to current thread for easy access
- Returns validation results and next steps

VALIDATION CHECKS:
1. Workflow has at least one action
2. Trigger is properly configured
3. All tool names are valid (from 594 available tools)
4. Required parameters are present
5. Placeholder syntax is correct ({{variable}})
6. No circular dependencies

EXAMPLE RESPONSE TO USER:
'✓ Your Daily Gmail Summary workflow is now published!

**Validation:** All checks passed
**Status:** Active
**Workflow ID:** wf_a3f8b2c1_1732029847
**Schedule:** Daily at 9:00 AM (UTC)
**Next Run:** Tomorrow at 9:00 AM
**Thread Link:** Added to this conversation

Your workflow will now:
1. Run automatically every morning at 9:00 AM
2. Get your unread Gmail messages
3. Generate an AI summary
4. Email you the digest

You can:
- View execution history: automation_get_execution_history()
- Pause schedule: automation_deactivate_workflow()
- Run manually: automation_execute_workflow()
- Edit in canvas: automation_open_workflow_in_canvas()'

PARAMETERS:
- slug='wf_xxx' (required, workflow to publish)
- thread_id=123 (optional, links to conversation)
- automation_title='My Workflow (Live)' (optional, custom name)
- schedule_cron='0 9 * * *' (optional, schedule)
- timezone='America/New_York' (optional, defaults to UTC)

WITHOUT SCHEDULING:
- If no schedule_cron provided, workflow is published as 'manual trigger only'
- User must run with automation_execute_workflow()
- Good for on-demand workflows or event-triggered workflows

thread_id.description: Thread ID to link the published automation to (usually the current thread)

automation_title.description: Optional custom title for the live automation (e.g., 'Email to Sheets (Production)'). If not provided, adds '(Live)' to workflow title.

schedule_cron.description: Optional cron expression for scheduling (e.g., '0 9 * * *' for daily at 9am, '0 */1 * * *' for hourly). If provided, automation will run on schedule.

timezone.description: Optional timezone for schedule (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'UTC'). Defaults to UTC.

returns.description: Publish result with validation status, automation_slug, scheduling info, and success message. Includes validation warnings/errors, next run time if scheduled, and thread linking confirmation.

examples.description: Publish workflow and schedule it to run hourly
Publish workflow without scheduling (manual execution only)

tools.name: automation_get_workflow_status
tools.description:
Get the current status of a workflow/automation including execution history, scheduling information, and success rate. Use this when user asks 'how is my workflow doing?', 'show me the status', 'is it running?', or 'when did it last run?'.

USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use this for high-level workflow health check
- Returns summary of workflow performance and current state
- Shows scheduling info, execution stats, and last run details
- Simpler than automation_get_execution_history() (shows summary, not full logs)
- Good for quick status updates

RESPONSE INCLUDES:
**Metadata:**
- automation_id, slug, title, description, category
- status: 'draft', 'active', 'inactive'
- created_at, updated_at

**Scheduling:**
- schedule_cron (if scheduled)
- timezone
- next_run_time (ISO timestamp)
- is_scheduled (true/false)

**Execution Stats:**
- total_executions (all-time count)
- successful_executions (success count)
- failed_executions (failure count)
- success_rate (percentage)
- currently_running (true/false)

**Last Execution:**
- last_execution_id
- last_execution_time (ISO timestamp)
- last_execution_duration (seconds)
- last_execution_status ('success'/'failure')
- last_execution_error (if failed)

EXAMPLE RESPONSE TO USER:
'Here's the status of your Daily Gmail Summary workflow:

🟢 **Status:** Active and running
📅 **Schedule:** Daily at 9:00 AM (America/New_York)
⏰ **Next Run:** Tomorrow at 9:00 AM (in 14 hours)

📊 **Performance:**
- Total Executions: 45
- Success Rate: 95.6% (43 successful, 2 failed)
- Average Duration: 4.1 seconds

🕐 **Last Run:**
- Time: 2 hours ago (Today at 9:00 AM)
- Duration: 4.2 seconds
- Status: ✓ Success
- Result: Processed 8 emails, sent summary

Your workflow is healthy and running smoothly!'

WHEN TO USE:
- User asks 'is my workflow working?'
- Quick health check
- Monitor after recent changes
- Check if workflow is scheduled vs manual
- See when it will run next

VS automation_get_execution_history():
- use get_workflow_status() for SUMMARY
- use get_execution_history() for DETAILED LOGS

slug.description: Workflow slug to check status for (e.g., 'workflow-1737052800')

returns.description: Complete status information including workflow metadata (title, status, schedule), execution stats (total runs, success rate, currently running), and last execution details (time, duration, status, error if failed). Also includes next run time if scheduled.
